prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No one cures macular degeneration, so the Main KPI of 196,000,000 patients cured is open work, though what exists must be stated honestly. The two approved geographic-atrophy drugs only slow lesion growth, by about 16 to 22 percent (pegcetacoplan) and 14 to 28 percent (avacincaptad pegol), with little change in best-corrected or low-luminance acuity, vision-function benefit only in post hoc analyses, repeated intravitreal injections and increased risk of progression to wet disease (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=%22geographic%20atrophy%22%20AND%20%28pegcetacoplan%20OR%20avacincaptad%29%20AND%20%28outcomes%20OR%20%22visual%20function%22%29&format=json&pageSize=5&resultType=core). Gene therapy targets injection burden rather than cure, with ABBV-RGX-314 the only phase 2-3 programme (671 participants) among otherwise phase 1 and 1-2 cell and gene studies, including autologous iPSC-RPE in 10 patients and hESC-RPE in 16; none is approved. Photoreceptor and RPE replacement remains unproven: a 2026 PNAS study states functional visual gains from iPSC-derived RPE are modest to date, and reviews cite poor cell survival and integration. Open source is two small image-classification repositories (https://api.github.com/search/repositories?q=macular+degeneration+OCT+deep+learning&per_page=10&sort=stars). Honest limit: anti-VEGF and complement inhibition are standard care and thoroughly published, so tasks on them are known answers; the open work is restoring lost photoreceptor and RPE function, which no approved or open solution does.
